thesis: Marvell is the number-two custom AI silicon franchise chasing Broadcom's jackpot: record Q1 FY2027 revenue of $2.418B (+28% y/y), Q2 guided to $2.7B, fiscal-2027 growth projected ~40% on 'exceptional' AI bookings across custom XPU, 800G/1.6T optics, and 51.2T switching, with custom chip revenue of $1.5B in FY2026 growing 20%+. The stock ran +130% into late June (aided by S&P 500 inclusion), then fell ~8% on July 7 as the index-buying wave ended and a Samsung-triggered sector selloff hit - leaving it at ~79x trailing earnings, priced roughly double what a disciplined DCF supports even after the drop.
catalysts: New custom XPU design-win announcements (the Broadcom-jackpot narrative)
FY2027 ~40% revenue growth delivery; FY2028 outlook already raised
risk_factors: Valuation: ~79x trailing earnings; the July 7 selloff (-7.5 to -8.75%) still leaves the price ~2x a disciplined DCF value
Broadcom competition: the custom-silicon market leader has deeper hyperscaler relationships and better economics; Marvell wins the deals Broadcom passes on
Custom-program concentration and cancellation opacity - same structural risk as AVGO with less diversification
AI-capex digestion hits every segment simultaneously (optics + switching + XPU)
Post-index-inclusion flows cut both ways; beta 2.20 with -8.49% weekly move (one source printed -22.11%)
